correctness.rationale: Edmonds graphic matroid independence inequalities are coordinate lower bounds and induced-subgraph rank upper bounds; in complete bipartite graph each rank subset indexed by a,b with normal Euclidean norm sqrt(ab). Averaging over edge-transitive S_p×S_q makes a scalar center c1 admissible, coordinate facets force c≥r, and rank facets force r≤(a+b-1)/(ab+sqrt(ab)); choosing c=r attains all. Derivative with t=sqrt(a) strictly favors increasing smaller shore up to p, except K2,2 equality, so reduce to f_p(b). The derivative in sqrt(b) has a unique turning point b*_p∈(Bp-1,Bp); exact two-candidate finite cutoff and p=2 b=10 follow, not a numerical fit. Active bicliques force EVERY coordinate of a radius-r incenter to equal r, so unique; connected-flat facet criterion gives contacting biclique count and four single-edge upper contacts when K2,2. Independently enumerated ALL bicliques for p=2..17 and q at/below/above cubic cutoff; original two-variable minimum agrees with two-term formula. Infinite results follow from algebra and facet arguments, not finite test.
